causalModel.founding: A Legion column was left unpaid at the recall. The column never marched home. The column's sons and grandsons keep the duty roster and the colours as an inheritance.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The camp stands on a bench on the hill above a junction of two tracks. The bench is out of sight of the Gideon road. A stream runs below the bench.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The men keep watches and wear the Legion colours. They take tolls from travellers and call each toll a levy.
causalModel.pressures: Gideon's governor will not pay to clear the camp. The toll company's officers would use the men for their own ends.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If Gideon offered the men a pardon and a wage, they would disband.

districts.notes: Four Legion tents in one dressed line on a hillside bench, a fire in front of them and a barricade on the track below.

why.what: The camp holds the tent line, its fire and the levy post. The levy post stands on the track.
why.whyHere: The column holds a track junction off the Gideon road, which lies 165 m east of the camp. Carts for Mile House of the Eagle must pass the junction. Carts for Swampmoth Town to the north must pass it too.
why.whySpot: The camp stands on the level bench on the hillside. The bench lies above the junction.
why.whyNeighbours: The track bends away to the west. The hill rises to the south-west. The tents are out of sight of every neighbouring place.
why.playerPurpose: The camp is hostile. The men ask for a levy on the track. The serjeant parleys before he fights.
why.microGeography: The camp stands on a narrow level bench on a hillside. The ground falls away to the stream and the track below.

parcels.orientationWhy: The command tent heads the tent line. Its open long side faces north, toward the brazier and the track below.

playerPurpose.note: The serjeant keeps a Legion duty roster in this tent. Men who still keep it are offered a pardon, if the wording allows one.
The toll office's boat schedules are kept in this tent. The bandits use them to choose which boats to rob.
The pay book lies on the campaign table, where a quest asks the player to read it.

why.what: This is the serjeant's command tent. A campaign table stands in it. The pay book lies on the table.
why.whyHere: The column keeps its orders, roster and accounts as the Legion taught. The serjeant keeps them in the command tent.
why.whySpot: The tent stands at the west end of the bench, at the head of the line.
why.whyNeighbours: The three sleeping tents stand in line beside the command tent. A brazier burns at the mouth of the command tent.
why.playerPurpose: The serjeant's tent holds the pay book. It also holds the toll office's schedules.
why.microGeography: The tent stands at the west end of the bench. The ground there is levelled for the tent and its brazier.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The command tent heads the line. The first squad's tent stands at its side, within call. Legion camps in Skyrim use the same spacing.

parcels.orientationWhy: The first sleeping tent's open gable faces north, toward the line walk. It is dressed on the command tent.

why.what: This is the first sleeping tent of the line. It stands next to the serjeant's tent.
why.whyHere: The column sleeps under issue canvas. Each squad has one tent, as the Legion taught.
why.whySpot: The tent stands beside the command tent on the bench. The men levelled this ground first.
why.whyNeighbours: The command tent heads the line. The brazier stands beyond the command tent.
why.playerPurpose: The first squad of the column keeps its kit here. The first squad of the column keeps its kit here.
why.microGeography: The tent has a levelled canvas floor. It stands on the bench beside the command tent.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The tent is pitched beside the command tent and the middle tent. All three stand in one dressed line, as Legion camps in Skyrim are pitched. The mined line template is vanilla:t0224. The template sets small tents 4.13 m apart at one yaw.

parcels.orientationWhy: The middle tent's open gable faces north. It stands square to the camp path that ends at it.

why.what: This is the middle sleeping tent. It stands at the head of the camp path.
why.whyHere: This is the second squad's canvas. It is pitched to the same line and the same yaw as the first tent.
why.whySpot: The tent stands in the middle of the bench. The camp path comes up from the track at this point.
why.whyNeighbours: Tents stand on either side of it. The camp path lies in front of it.
why.playerPurpose: This sleeping tent stands at the head of the camp path. It is the first tent that a player reaches.
why.microGeography: The tent has a levelled canvas floor. It stands in the middle of the line.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The tent stands in the middle of the dressed line. It is a tent's width from its neighbours on either side. Legion camps in Skyrim use the same spacing.

parcels.orientationWhy: The last tent's open gable faces north, toward the barricade below. It is the last of the line.

why.what: This is the last sleeping tent. It stands at the east end of the line, by the banner.
why.whyHere: This is the third squad's canvas. The line ends here because the bench ends here.
why.whySpot: The tent stands at the east end of the bench. The ground starts to fall to the stream there.
why.whyNeighbours: The banner stands beyond the tent. The levy post stands below on the track.
why.playerPurpose: This is the last sleeping tent, nearest the barricade. The men sleep here after their turn on watch.
why.microGeography: The tent has a levelled canvas floor. It stands at the east end of the bench, above the camp path.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The tent ends the dressed line. It is pitched at the line's spacing from the middle tent. The bench ends a few steps further east.

routes.why: A trodden way climbs from the Mile House track to the end of the tent line. Travellers must use this path to enter the camp.
The line walk runs along the front of the tent line. It runs from the camp path to the mouth of the command tent.
A short step leaves the line walk. It leads to the mouth of the first sleeping tent.
A short step leaves the line walk. It leads to the mouth of the middle sleeping tent.

occupants.cultureRole: The serjeant parleys before he fights.
The band are the column's surviving descendants.

approaches.sequence: A traveller coming east along the track sees the banners on the hill first. Next the tent line comes into view. Last comes the barricade, which blocks half the track below the tents.
approaches.wayfinding: The track runs under the bench. A footpath climbs from the barricade to the fire.

approaches.sequence: A traveller coming down the track from the north reaches the stream. The barricade stands at the junction ahead. The tents stand above it on the right.
approaches.wayfinding: The junction lies at the stream. The barricade stands a few steps west of the junction.

networkTerminals.why: The camp path leaves the Mile House track below the bench. It runs east along the track to the end of the barricade. It then climbs through the gap in the stakes to the tent line.

combatSpaces.why: The trodden ground lies between the tent line and the fire. The level ground on the hillside lies here.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The source is the catalogue record The Broke Column (camp, M1). The record gives four Legion tents pitched in a line.
scaleGrounding.why: One command tent and three sleeping tents make up the camp. They house a serjeant and what is left of a column.

candidates.why: A bench stands on the hillside above the track junction. An 8 m pad there cuts and fills at most half a metre.
This candidate is the plotted anchor. It lies on the stream at the track junction.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The builder rejected it. It lies on the stream at the track junction. The ground is wet and poorly drained.
